name: Syndrome with Woolly Hair

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Woolly Hair Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of tightly curled, fine, and brittle hair with a woolly texture
Hair shaft abnormalities demonstrated by light or electron microscopy
Presence of cardiac abnormalities such as arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC)
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of woolly hair with hair shaft abnormalities plus either cardiac anomalies or positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis in some cases; cardiac evaluation is essential due to risk of cardiomyopathy.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Tightly curled, fine, brittle woolly hair
searchTerms: woolly hair that is fragile and curly

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal hair shaft morphology (e.g., twisting, kinking)

searchTerms: heart rhythm problems from muscle disease

rare.symptomName: Woolly hair with associated ectodermal dysplasia features
searchTerms: woolly hair with skin and nail abnormalities
ectodermal dysplasia features with curly hair
hair and skin changes including woolly hair

rare.symptomName: Severe cardiac arrhythmias leading to syncope
searchTerms: heart rhythm disturbances leading to passing out
areas of hair missing since birth

laboratory: Hair shaft microscopy showing twisting and kinking
Genetic testing identifying mutations in desmosomal protein genes (e.g., DSP, JUP)
imaging: Cardiac MRI showing right ventricular dilation and fibrofatty replacement
genetic: Mutations in genes encoding desmosomal proteins such as plakoglobin (JUP), desmoplakin (DSP), plakophilin-2 (PKP2)
other: Electrocardiogram abnormalities including epsilon waves and ventricular arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Woolly hair with palmoplantar keratoderma and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
Woolly hair with dilated left ventricular cardiomyopathy

redFlags: Sudden cardiac death or syncope in young patients
Severe hair fragility with associated skin infections
references: Norgett EE, et al. 'Recessive mutation in desmoplakin causes dilated cardiomyopathy, woolly hair and keratoderma.' Nat Genet. 2000.
McKoy G, et al. 'Identification of a deletion in plakoglobin in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy with palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair (Naxos disease).' Lancet. 2000.
